title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector support for conflict-affected IDP returnees and host communities in Jardega Jarte woreda of Horo Gudru zone, Oromia Region

description.narrative: ltpgtAligned with the EHF 2025 Third Reserve Allocation objective—to deliver integrated, time-critical humanitarian assistance for returning IDPs in western Oromia-this project proposes a coordinated multi-sector response addressing acute, life-saving needs across Nutrition, WASH, ES/NFI, Agriculture, and Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC). ANE’s approach ensures rapid stabilization, early recovery, and a smooth handover to development actors through localized, protection-centered interventions. The project targets both returning IDPs and host communities across Jardega Jirate woreda supporting approximately ltbgt28,500lt/bgt individuals with a package that combines cash and in-kind assistance based on market feasibility.ltbrgtCore interventions include:ltbrgtNutrition: Screening for more than ltbgt13500 lt/bgtunder 5 children and pregnant and lactating women(PLW) will take place. Strengthening stabilization and OTP centers is prioritized with enhancing the capacity to admit SAM cases to SC( 62 SAM admissions to SC are expected), capacity-building for 60 health care workers, and IYCF-E promotion. WASH: Rehabilitation of 4 community water points including 1 ltbgtsolarization of bore hole in sute kata ali kebele of Jardega Jartelt/bgt woreda which is currently working with fuel generator and sometimes interrupted due shortage of fuel, household water treatment provision for 400 HHs, and construction of inclusive sanitation facilities to ensure safe, equitable access to clean water and improved hygiene.ES/NFI: Provision of essential shelter repair kits with cash for labor cost and some inputs to 415 highly vulnerable households, where 353HH will receive standard ESRK while 62HHs will receive ESRK for inclusion persons with disabilities and most vulnerable HHs Capacity building training for the carpenters will also complement the support for sustainable repair of damaged shelters. Agriculture and Livelihoods: Improved agriculture seeds and agriculture tools will be provided for 1,800 individuals and in addition to that 300 most vulnerable, women led households will receive 5 shoats each complemented by capacity strengthening of the development army and model farmers to boost food security and livelihood recovery. MPC: Flexible cash assistance to address essential household needs with dignity and strengthen local market functionality.ltbrgtProtection and GBV risk mitigation are mainstreamed across all activities through GBV/PSEA training, functional feedback and complaint mechanisms, and provision of dignity kits for 400 women and girls with integrating into WASH platforms. Inclusive targeting ensures equitable access for persons with disabilities, older persons, and other at-risk groups.ltbrgtA robust monitoring and accountability system will track outcomes through post-distribution monitoring (PDM), WASH quality assessments, and real-time beneficiary feedback. Coordination with relevant clusters and government offices will guide modality adaptation and risk management, particularly in areas affected by access constraints or market disruptions.ltbrgtSustainability is embedded through handover of rehabilitated assets and community structures to woreda offices and WASHCOs, ensuring continuity beyond the project period. By bridging urgent humanitarian needs with localized recovery pathways, this intervention directly contributes to EHF’s strategic goal of restoring dignity, resilience, and self-reliance among conflict-affected populations in Western Oromia.lt/pgt
